uncited: **Volume Data:** A 3-D signal sampled on a BCC or FCC grid.
**Smooth Surface Coefficients:** A signed integer coefficient for each voxel in the transition region, representing the sub-voxel distance between the voxel center and the object boundary.
The grid is defined by its Voronoi cells.
*   Two voxels are connected if they share a common face.
*   Two faces are connected if they share a common edge.
*   Two edges are connected if they share a common vertex.
*   **Object Surface:** The set of faces between object voxels and non-object voxels.
*   **Smooth Surface Coefficients:** A signed integer $c \in [-128, 127]$ assigned to each voxel in contact with the object surface.
All possible ray directions are partitioned into regions corresponding to the yard directions perpendicular to the faces of the Voronoi polyhedron.
*   **BCC Grid:** 24 directional regions.
*   Each region is defined by a basis of three vectors $\{\vec{A}, \vec{B}, \vec{C}\}$ corresponding to faces of the Voronoi polyhedron sharing a common vertex.
**Step 1: Compute Smooth Surface Coefficients**
Apply an edge detector operator based on geometric moments to the volume data.
This estimates the sub-voxel distance between the voxel center and the object boundary.
Given the ray direction vector $\vec{d}$, identify which of the 24 (BCC) or 20 (FCC) directional regions it falls into.
Decompose the line vector $\vec{PQ}$ components $\{n_a, n_b, n_c\}$ in the basis $\{\vec{A}, \vec{B}, \vec{C}\}$ of the identified region.
**Step 4: Trace the Ray (Minimize Rhombus Area)**
Trace the line by advancing from one voxel to the next, minimizing the area of the rhombus $R$ (the rhombic base of the prism containing all line beam points).
Project the grid points onto a plane $N$ orthogonal to the line $\vec{PQ}$.
At each step, select the next voxel such that the area of the rhombus $R$ formed by the current and next beam points is minimized.
*   **Degenerate Input:** The method assumes the ray direction is not parallel to any basis vector face normal, which would make the decomposition ambiguous.
Allows robust definition of discrete curves and surfaces.
Enables sub-voxel deformation by changing coefficients.
*   When topological correctness is critical (e.g., medical imaging where missing a surface is unacceptable).
*   When sub-voxel surface representation is needed for smooth rendering or collision detection.
*   When computational resources allow for the overhead of resampling and basis decomposition.
*   For simple scenes where cubic grid topological defects are negligible or handled by thicker rays.
*   When real-time performance on very low-end hardware is required and the overhead of BCC/FCC processing is prohibitive.
The paper describes a ray-tracing and object description method for objects sampled in BCC and FCC grids, which are well-known in crystallography.
